note: One natural-language user query per capability, for END-TO-END routing evaluation: given the query, does a model using the MCP server actually invoke the right capability? This is NOT search-eval.json. That fixture measures whether the correct answer lands in the top N of searchCapability's ranking — pure scoring, keyed by method+path. This one measures whether a model, handed those results, PICKS correctly. The two can disagree in both directions: a model can rescue a rank-3 answer, or choose wrong when the right one ranked 1. Design rule for every query here: phrase the need as a user would, and do NOT echo the capability's own distinctive tokens. A query that restates the capability name makes the test pass trivially and measures nothing. These 77 cover the capabilities search-eval.json has no query for (77 tm); the other 165 already have one there and should be reused rather than rewritten. KNOWN CAVEAT, so results are read honestly: 29 of these queries share a word with their own capability name — almost always the ENTITY noun (folder, plan, report, comment). That is legitimate, because a user asking about a folder does say 'folder', and stripping it would produce queries no real user would type. But it does make those 29 easier than the rest, so a per-case pass is not uniformly hard. The cases carrying a `trap` field are the deliberately hard ones: near-duplicate siblings, a scope difference (one test vs the whole project), or a misleading capability name.
